documentation.content:
A NODE IS NOT READY.

Impact: every pod on that node is unreachable or being rescheduled. Capacity has silently dropped.

First command:
  kubectl get nodes
  kubectl describe node NODE | grep -A10 Conditions

Read the conditions:
  MemoryPressure=True  -> node is out of memory, pods are being evicted
  DiskPressure=True    -> disk full, image pulls will start failing
  Ready=Unknown        -> the kubelet stopped reporting (crash or network partition)

If you are running SPOT VMs (this project's default), the most likely cause is
PREEMPTION. Google reclaimed the node with 30 seconds notice. That is the trade
you accepted for the 60-91% discount, and it is why minReplicas is 2 and there
is a topology spread constraint.

GKE node auto-repair handles most of this automatically. If it does not:
  kubectl cordon NODE
  kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

If the drain HANGS, check PodDisruptionBudgets:
  kubectl get pdb -A        <-- ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS: 0 is the culprit
